TextView.android:text: Tap to understand what each level does
OFF — fast compile, no IR passes applied
When OFF: OLLVM clang compiles normally — fast, no passes. When ON: all 8 IR obfuscation passes run at the intensity you select below.
Every pass at absolute maximum. Near-impenetrable output.
All 8 at near-peak intensity. Defeats most decompiler analysis.
All 8 at extreme intensity. Heavy protection, manageable build time.
All 8 at heavy intensity — matches the original default settings.
All 8 passes, balanced intensity. Best for daily production builds.
All 8 passes, moderate intensity. Faster builds, still solid protection.
All 8 passes, standard intensity. Quick builds, meaningful hardening.
All 8 passes, minimal intensity. Very fast builds, light hardening.
All 8 passes, baseline intensity. Near-native build speed.
Pick exactly which of the 8 passes run on your build
Full control. Toggle any pass on or off. Tap a pass name to learn what it does.
Tap a pass name to see exactly what it does. Toggle to enable or disable it. Changes save instantly.
Replaces math ops with complex equivalents
XOR-encrypts all string literals in the binary
Bloats the function graph with chopped blocks
Hides which function is being called
Hides global data access through indirection

All 8 levels use every obfuscation technique. Only the intensity parameters change — bcf_prob controls how many blocks are obfuscated, bcf_loop and split_num control how deeply. Higher = harder output, longer compile. Lower = faster build, lighter output.
